purpose: Layer B for report_methodology. The 'items' list classifies TIMING-6/TIMING-7 clock-pair findings by named clock pair; the 'methodology_items' list classifies every remaining Warning/Advisory rule. Critical Warnings that are not reclassified here stay in Layer A unchanged.
notes: This file does not create a set_clock_groups, a false path or a waiver. It records, per named pair, which evidence must be re-read from this round's reports before the finding may be called reviewed methodology.

UG903 (Using Constraints) Exceptions Priority: clock groups override false paths, max delays and multicycles, but set_bus_skew is never overridden by them; report_cdc still analyses ignored/max-delay paths. That is why declaring a pair asynchronous would still not hide a Critical CDC - and why this file refuses to declare one while Critical CDC exists.

optional: true means the rule may legitimately be absent in another design shape; absence is still printed in the ledger, presence must still be reviewed. It never weakens the check on a finding that IS present.

items.structure: clk_pl_0 is the PS PL clock output (measured source pin zynq_ultra_ps_e_0/.../PS8_i/PLCLK[0], 10.000 ns, 63388 driven registers); pcie_user_clk is a generated clock from the GT quad (u_pcie_ip/.../gt_top_i/.../phy_clk_i/bufg_gt_userclk, 8.000 ns) whose ultimate reference is sys_clk through qpll0outclk_out[0] -> GTHE4_CHANNEL_TXOUTCLK[3]. Two independent physical sources, neither constrained against the other; there is no clock group anywhere in this build (report_exceptions: Clock Group rows = 0).
items.rationale: TIMING-6/TIMING-7 say 'related but no common primary clock / no common node'. That is the signature of legitimate CDC structures tying two independent clocks together (AXI-Lite clock converter, XPM async FIFOs, the probe meter snapshot, the Gray timestamp), not of a missing constraint. The pair may be called reviewed only while all of the following are re-proved in the same round: no Critical CDC and no uncovered HIGH endpoint exists (checked in code, not asserted here), the named project exceptions that cross clock domains still resolve to non-empty object lists with their requirement values, and neither report_exceptions -ignored nor -scope_override lists them, and both interaction directions are present in report_clock_interaction.

items.structure: clkout2 is the VPHY RX video clock: a child of the hdmi_rx_clk_p reference in the Clock Summary, 6.734 ns / 148.5 MHz, and the clock report_cdc names for the launch flops of the three u_hdmi_probe crossings declared here. clk_pl_0 is the PS PLCLK[0] output, 10.000 ns. Two independent physical sources; the only registered path from one to the other in this direction is the probe diagnostic level, which rtl/sc7f0_hdmi_probe.v now captures in clkout2 first and then synchronises with a 3-FF ASYNC_REG chain in clk_pl_0.
items.rationale: TIMING-6/7/8 say 'related (timed together) but no common primary clock / no common node / no common expandable period' for this pair, and in round 26111202 the same pair also held that round's WNS (-2.760 ns at a 0.002 ns requirement) because the crossing was fed through the vendor's combinational output with no exception at all. That part is now a design fix, not a paperwork fix: a source-domain register, a first-stage chain that measures ASYNC_REG in the routed netlist, and one exception per signal written from that register to chain[0]. The pair may be called reviewed only while every one of those facts is re-measured in the same round: each of the three crossings resolves, carries ASYNC_REG, spans exactly two clock domains, keeps its internal chain stages analysed (an exception that grew to -from-clock would show up as zero analysed paths), keeps its feed-in timed at clkout2's own period rather than at a 0.002 ns async requirement, and is neither ignored nor scope-overridden; the probe meter / Gray / DPRAM max-delay and bus-skew constraints this design depends on are still in force with their measured values; no clock group may exist anywhere; and the harness refuses this reclassification at all while any Critical CDC row or uncovered HIGH endpoint is left in Layer A. report_clock_interaction's own aggregate string 'Partial False Path (unsafe)' is NOT the evidence - it is the reason this entry demands the per-crossing measurements above instead of trusting the table, because one exception per crossing is exactly what 'partial' means here. What this entry still cannot see is spelled out in missing-claim form: a NEW crossing between these two clocks that already arrives ASYNC_REG-synchronised is not counted by it; what closes that hole is report_cdc itself (an unsynchronised or combinational crossing comes back as Critical CDC-10/11/12/13 and Layer A refuses the round, and any new Warning row must be claimed by an entry in sc7f0_cdc_review.json or Layer B fails).

items.structure: phy_rxoutclk is the GTH RX output clock of the vid_phy_controller (Clock Summary: a child of GTHE4_CHANNEL_RXOUTCLK[0], 6.734 ns); clk_pl_0 is the PS PLCLK[0], 10.000 ns. In this direction the design crosses (a) the probe's three channel-valid diagnostic levels, now source-registered on clk_rxout and then 3-FF synchronised, and (b) the frequency-meter request/acknowledge/toggle-ack crossings plus the 32-bit snapshot bus, which the project constraint probe_meter_max_delay times with set_max_delay -datapath_only 10.0.
items.rationale: Same class of finding as clkout2__clk_pl_0 and the same reason it was red in round 26111202: three CDC-10 Critical rows with Exception = None (launch flop u_vid_phy_controller/inst/xpm_array_single_DRU_CTRL_in_sync_inst/syncstages_ff_reg[2][1]) and -1.631 ns at a 0.002 ns requirement, i.e. combinational logic in front of the pl_clk0 first stage. The fix is a register in phy_rxoutclk plus one exception per signal from that flop to chain[0]; the meter crossings keep their measured max delay. The pair is graded, not waived: ASYNC_REG, two domains, internal chain stages still analysed, feed-in timed at phy_rxoutclk's own period, no ignored or scope-overridden exception, no clock group, and no Critical CDC row anywhere in the round.

methodology_items.structure: Missing input/output delay on asynchronous pads, as check_timing grouped them in round 26111202: 0 input ports at HIGH and 8 at MEDIUM (hdmi_rx_5v_det, hdmi_rx_ddc_scl/_sda, hdmi_tx_ddc_scl/_sda, hdmi_tx_hpd_in, hdmi_tx_refclk_rdy, sys_rst_n - all already covered by a named -from <port> exception); 6 output ports at HIGH of which 2 have no constraint at all (hdmi_rx_ddc_scl, hdmi_rx_ddc_sda) and 4 already sit at MEDIUM behind a named exception (hdmi_rx_hpd_out, hdmi_tx_tmds_clk_p, user_led_dma_active, user_led_pcie_link_up).
methodology_items.rationale: Eleven of the thirteen ports are async or quasi-static levels where an invented delay number would be a fake constraint; each is itemised one port at a time in sc7f0_cdc_review.json io_items and written in constraints/sc7f0_async_io.xdc, restricted to the measured first-stage cells on the input side and ending at the pad on the output side. The two HIGH rows that remained were the RX DDC output direction, and they are now named per port (async_out_hdmi_rx_ddc_scl / _sda). The mechanism is not new: the four output ports already at MEDIUM are there because the same one-command-per-port shape moved them out of HIGH, so the next round either reproduces that for the DDC pair or the exception did not resolve - both outcomes are measured, not assumed. The TX TMDS clock pad stays unresolved because it is still driven by the VPHY (see tx_tmds_clock_pad).
methodology_items.missing_evidence: Re-read TIMING-18 and check_timing on a round built with constraints/sc7f0_async_io.xdc as it now stands: no_input_delay HIGH must stay 0 and no_output_delay HIGH must fall from 6 to 4 with hdmi_rx_ddc_scl/_sda appearing in the MEDIUM false-path group instead. Then close io_items rx_ddc_scl, rx_ddc_sda and tx_tmds_clock_pad.
